_notes: game_state added locally from NVRAM captured on an ALP4K cabinet either side of a 2-player game.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x02110A24: the game ended 9,116,750 / 8,923,670 and
those landed at 0x02110A24 and 0x02110A2C, with players 3 and 4 zero and the high word of each
slot zero throughout.
This is not where the other Stern SAM maps put them -- 24 and X-Men both use 0x021109E4, which
stayed zero here through a real game. The score address is per-ROM; do not carry it across.
player_count at 0x02110900 read 1 before and 2 after, the same address 24 and X-Men use. That
field does appear to be shared across SAM.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent bytes in CPU RAM at 0x0003006C and 0x0003006D, the
same shape X-Men uses at 0x00030AE4/0x00030AE5 -- player low, ball high. Found by counting rather
than by value: over one 4-player game the player byte completed 1->2->3 three times, once per
ball, and the ball byte once, its single completion landing on the player's second cycle and the
player's last landing on 9,348,440, which was player 1's final score.
The four scores of that game, 9,348,440 / 3,377,120 / 3,152,920 / 6,529,100, read back exactly
where this map declares them, so the 8-byte stride is now confirmed on four players rather than
inferred from two.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 1,094-frame recording of live memory spanning an
operator-menu session and a full two-player game. The same session confirmed by measurement the
previously derived ball_count and max_credits: set to 5 and 9 in the menu, adjustment records at
indices 32 and 34 moved 3 to 5 and 30 to 9 with their check bytes.
game_over at 0x00034C7E reads 100 in attract and 0 in play, flipping at the exact frame the game
started -- the same frame credits hit zero -- and back at game over. Any non-zero value decodes
as game over, so no mask is needed.
credits at 0x0211100C, the third SAM game measured at that same address: it rose as coins were
inserted and stepped down once per player entering the two-player game.
tilted at 0x00038D24 is active-low: 1 from game start onward, 0 for exactly the eleven samples
in which player 1's scoring sat still six seconds before the ball ended -- the only such plateau
in the game -- recovering the moment the next ball began. Declared with invert. Caveat recorded
honestly: before the first game of the session the byte also reads 0, so a consumer polling it
in attract sees tilted=true; it is meaningful only while a game is running. 0x00038CDA behaves
identically but also drops at game end -- 'ball live and not tilted' -- noted here in case that
shape is ever the more useful one.
bytes have read zero in every image captured, so the width is taken from the record's
The record is 36 bytes with the checksum at +32, so four bytes sit between the 4-byte score at
+24 and the checksum. They read zero in every image captured (163 records across five games)
and their purpose is not established: they are consistent with the upper half of a 64-bit score,
but this game's champion-threshold table at 0x021024F8 stores its thresholds as 4-byte values
with a complement check byte, which is what a 32-bit score would be compared against. The score
is therefore declared as 4 bytes until a value above 2^32 is observed or the ROM is disassembled.
